title: Pre-Analysis — Chromate-Free Protection Scheme Against the Bonded Joint Finding
abstract: Closed work order that examined the chromate-free protection scheme for lower shell repairs and stopped it at design freeze over the resistivity of the new primer at bonding lands.

sections.objective: Establish whether the chromate-free protection scheme could be released to repair stations as written, and in particular whether the higher resistivity of the new primer at bonding lands is covered by the existing repair drawings or needs a change to each of them. The scheme was otherwise ready and several operators were waiting for it.
sections.findings_summary: The scheme is sound and the corrosion performance is equivalent or better, but the bonding behaviour is not the same and the consequences run wider than expected. The new primer must be removed locally at every bonding land, which the repair drawings do not currently say because the chromated primer did not need it. That is a change to a large number of drawings rather than to the scheme, and it is the reason the design was frozen rather than released. Two further findings. The surface preparation task carries the time limits between preparation, sol-gel and primer, and those limits are short enough that a repair station without a mixed primer ready will simply exceed them; the task says so but the scheme summary does not. And a second, water-borne proposal is in circulation for a different regulatory driver, which raises the question of whether operators end up controlling three qualified schemes.
sections.next_steps: Hold the design frozen pending the agency finding on bonded joint resistivity. Prepare the repair drawing change as a single package rather than drawing by drawing. Raise the three-scheme question with the proposal owner before the water-borne route goes any further.

similarity_seeds: chromated primer withdrawal at a repair station
sol-gel preparation replacing a tank conversion process

tasks.title: Establish the bonding behaviour of the new primer at a land
Count the repair drawings that would need a change
Check the interaction with the water-borne proposal

evidence.similarity_note: Found by entity linking on the splice plate and collar part numbers that both documents carry.

expected_findings.rationale: The restoration scheme instructs that bonding lands are masked, but the acceptance for a land that has been primed and then cleaned back is not stated anywhere. Until it is, a repair station has no way of proving the land is acceptable.
expected_findings.resolution: Include the land acceptance in the repair drawing change package.

evidence.similarity_note: Found by entity linking on the splice plate and protective sleeve part numbers the task calls out.

expected_findings.rationale: The preparation task carries the time limits correctly, but the scheme summary a repair station reads first does not mention them. A station that begins preparation before mixing the primer will exceed them and will not know it has.
expected_findings.resolution: Add the time limits to the scheme summary as well as to the task.

evidence.similarity_note: Surfaced by similarity alone. The two documents describe the same repair areas in the same words but are driven by different regulations and share no identifier beyond the chapter.

expected_findings.rationale: A water-borne primer proposal is in circulation for an emissions driver rather than a chemicals one. If both are qualified, an operator with three schemes has three sets of drawings to control and no rule about which applies where.
expected_findings.resolution: Raise the three-scheme question before the water-borne route is qualified.

type_data.conclusion: Closed with the design frozen. The scheme cannot be released until the bonded joint acceptance exists.
